tasks.goal: Variable-level aggregation with consensus, coverage and confidence (VocationalScoring aggregates at dimension level today).
validation: F04/F05 parity with the reference engine
tasks.notes: Red first (commit e2548aee: naive aggregation, 12/22 tests fail on the defect symptom), then the fix. V360Aggregation: per source per variable the mean of F01-normalized answers -> F02/F03/F04 IntegrateSources over weights.v360_sources -> F05 Confidence360; the aggregate map is produced in the rule set's DECLARED variable order. Coverage is the reference's (sum of rater-source weights, what F05 consumes); ITEM coverage is recorded separately on a per-variable audit and warned on, because the two fail differently. V1 is SELF-ONLY, so consensus degenerates: one rater -> consensus None, confidence index null, global NOT_DETERMINABLE, warning V360_SINGLE_RATER -- no spread is manufactured. The global confidence is F05 applied once at instrument level (the GLOBAL arm of open question 7; F06's relevance-weighted index is the other arm and already ships beside it). Reads go through VocationalResponseLoader, VocationalWriter.LoadGroupsAsync lifted verbatim so there is ONE query for 'the student's 360 responses'; the variable code is read from vocational_responses.dimensionKey and, if FM-CF-006 seeds it elsewhere, NOTHING matches and the run degrades to NO_DATA rather than scoring something wrong. NoData stays the fallback and the selection is explicit (a named delegation, not an empty query): no rater group, or no response carrying a rules.v360_variables code, yields the empty map / NOT_DETERMINABLE / careerfit360 0.0 run of today. DI now registers VocationalV360Adapter; behaviour is unchanged until the items exist. P4–P6 INTEGRATION (branch careerfit/p4-p6): the aggregator's per-variable trail (V360VariableAudit) reached only as far as the adaptation and was dropped in Assemble, so the coverage / consensus detail arrived at the run as warning PROSE. It is now carried on InputQuality and persisted as careerfit_runs."inputQuality" -> v360_variables / v360_instrument, and FM-CF-010 records F01–F05 beside it as v360_formula_steps. V360VariableAudit gained SourceScores (F01's output per rater source, F02's input) and V360Adaptation gained Instrument (the instrument-level arm of F02–F05, where the run's one careerfit360_confidence label is produced).

tasks.goal: CareerFit360 per-family relevance weighting (F06) from rules.families[].v360_rules; IND excluded in V1.
validation: F06 parity; base_weight carried on the rule, not the schema gap
tasks.notes: F06 parity at 1e-9 over six synthetic aggregate sets x 14 families, per-variable combined_weight included: the weight is base_weight x relevance READ OFF THE RULE (rules.families[].v360_rules[code].base_weight, required by the loader since FM-CF-004), pinned by a test that perturbs the rule and watches the catalogue entry stay put, and by one that shows the same variable weighing differently in two families (IND relevance 3 in family 4, 2 in family 1). IND is EXCLUDED in V1 as a NAMED exclusion (V360Aggregation.ExcludedInV1) at the point the evidence is read, not a silent filter: P36 is a 20-industry selection vector and a per-family scalar needs an industry -> family projection TIMS has not delivered; the exclusion is recorded on every run (V360_IND_EXCLUDED) and a test proves removing IND still leaves every scorable family with weighted BASE rules. The rule set is untouched -- when the projection arrives, deleting the exclusion is the whole change. P35 (RANK) is NOT decided here (open question 5): it is recognised, recorded as not scored, and its weight is entirely the rule set's -- base_weight 0 in the catalogue and no family rule in 1.0.0-draft.1, so it contributes nothing today. P4–P6 INTEGRATION: each family's F06-weighted variables, with their base_weight × relevance, are what FM-CF-011's explainability payload surfaces as that family's 360 evidence and as its 360 modulators.

tasks.notes: P1–P3 integration (branch careerfit/p1-p3) ships the orchestrator half: CareerFitEvaluator (read → adapt → rules → EvaluateOwner per scorable family → AssignRelativeFit → write), CareerFitInputReader (one RLS read session; fail-closed CareerFitInputException per missing instrument), CareerFitRunWriter (run + 14 family rows in one transaction, the student's tenant on the run), and the audit shipped with the scores as evaluate_owner's audit_inputs / convergence_detail / critical_gaps / mil_relative_strengths per family. EvaluateCore reproduces the reference at 0.0 deviation. 360 is NoData (careerfit360 0, NOT_DETERMINABLE, SOLID is the convergence ceiling). The per-formula-step ledger the acceptance names shipped on branch careerfit/audit: CareerFitAuditLedger adds careerfit_family_results.audit -> formula_steps, one record per F01–F23 APPLICATION the evaluation actually executed (F07/F08/F09 per contributing route factor, F10 per route, F11, F12/F13 per competency rule with a scored role, F14, F15, F16, F17 per MIL subtest, F18 per personality route, F19, F06, F20, F22 per convergence instrument, F23 only where F22 did not already answer STRONG, F21 once ranked), each naming the step, its inputs, its output and the governing rule or threshold with its provenance — 39–56 records per family, 709 for one run of the sample student. F01–F05 are the 360 AGGREGATION pipeline and execute only once FM-CF-007 lands. §21 itself is not among the vendored sources, so the granularity is read off sheet 13_FORMULAS_ENGINE's own subscripts and evaluate_owner's order of operations; if TIMS delivers §21 and it disagrees, CareerFitAuditLedger is the only thing that changes. NO new table: the ledger rides in the existing audit jsonb because every read of it is 'the whole derivation for this (run, family)' — the row being fetched anyway — while a table would cost ~700 tuples per run per student, forever, for queries nobody makes; so no policy, no GRANT, no fixture-schema and no apply-order change. EvaluateOwner is untouched and the parity fixture still regenerates byte-identical at 0.0 deviation. Still open for this slice: the endpoints (FM-CF-012). P4–P6 INTEGRATION (branch careerfit/p4-p6) closes this slice's engine half, so the status is now completed. The merge added what the ledger could not have before: F01–F05, the 360 aggregation pipeline that FM-CF-007's aggregator turned on. They are recorded ONCE PER STUDENT on careerfit_runs."inputQuality" -> v360_formula_steps, not fourteen times on the family rows, because the aggregate map is GLOBAL — built before any family is scored, and F06 is the first 360 formula a family subscripts. So the family ledger's count stays derivable from the rule set alone, and the run ledger's count is derivable from the variable trail beside it (Σ over scored variables of its answering-source count + 4, plus the instrument arm's 4). No DDL: inputQuality is already a jsonb column. STILL OPEN: the endpoints (FM-CF-012).

tasks.goal: Explainability payload: structured evidence only (strengths, gaps, winning routes, gates, convergence, modulators). No percentage next to a family.
validation: contract test: no field named *percent*/*probability* on a family result (asserted by reflection over every public type in the namespace AND over the serialised JSON)
tasks.notes: Built on branch careerfit/p4-p6, NOT by the explain slice: branch careerfit/explain was created and never committed to (it points at the same SHA as careerfit/p1-p3), so services/api/src/FormMaps.Api/Contracts/CareerFit did not exist and the integration brief's “ensure the payload surfaces the real 360 evidence” had nothing to ensure. CareerFitExplanation is a PURE PROJECTION over the run FM-CF-010 persisted — gates, convergence and per-instrument support, the winning PCA and personality routes, the critical competency gaps, the MIL band and relative strengths, the 360 evidence, and structured modulators — so it computes nothing and cannot disagree with the scores it explains. It carries NO family-level fit scalar at all (no careerfit_absolute, careerfit_relative, pca_index, mil_fit or route score), which is stronger than the stated validation: guardrail 3's point is that a 0–100 number beside a career family reads as a likelihood whatever it is called, so what the payload carries about “how well” is the ORDINAL rank and categorical labels. The name check ran RED on its first execution and found the raw LIA Percentile on the MIL block; it was removed rather than the assertion weakened — open question 1 (what population the MIL percentiles are normed on) is unanswered, while the BAND is the workbook's own presentation category and survives a re-norm. 360 has its own shape because it is the one instrument that may be wholly absent: Determinable is read from the RUN's v360_source, never from the length of a family's variable list, and carries either the no-evidence reason or the single-rater reason in words. Both naive readings were proven RED with the naive code in place — a family that weights none of the variables a student answered (PB is weighted by no family in 1.0.0-draft.1) is still a student who completed a 360, and SELF-ONLY is neither “no evidence” nor “confident evidence”. MODULATORS are surfaced as structured facts (MIL relative strengths, and each 360 variable's base_weight × relevance, heaviest first) and NOT as the rule set's per-family v360_route_modulators_text, which is free Spanish prose naming route flavours the engine does not score and which P1–P3 does not parse into CareerFitRules. NOT here: any HTTP surface, route, authorization or feature flag — FM-CF-012 owns those.

tasks.notes: THE SEVEN ARE DERIVED, NOT GUESSED. The legacy career surface, as apps/web actually calls it, is eleven method+path pairs in two files (services/careerService.ts :21 :33 :42 :52 :57 :65 :73 :84 :98 :107 :116, services/timsService.ts :8). Exactly ONE of them is a CareerFit question — POST /api/v1/careers/score, the manifest's own legacyBaseline and FM-CF-013's shadow target. The other ten are the 370-role CATALOGUE, its admin CRUD and favourites; V1 CareerFit scores fourteen FAMILIES and has no career catalogue at all (careerfit-schema.sql: 'no per-career / per-subfamily rows'), so those ten STAY on Node and next.config.ts rewrites none of them. The seven are that one legacy question split along the seams the engine actually has: legacy /score both SCORES and RETURNS and every apps/web caller uses it as a READ on mount (CareerMatches.tsx:25, StatCards.tsx:106, CareerMatchHub.tsx:45, careers/compare/page.tsx:16, PCAReports.tsx:48), but a run is IMMUTABLE, so scoring is POST /careerfit/evaluate/{userId} and reading is GET /careerfit/results/{userId} and GET /careerfit/runs/{runId}; the legacy response's explanatory half (types/tims.ts profileSummary/breakdown) is FM-CF-011's payload on GET .../results/{userId}/explanation and .../runs/{runId}/explanation; immutability makes the run history a real question (GET .../results/{userId}/runs, the read careerfit_runs_userId_createdAt_idx exists for); and legacy GET /careers/clusters becomes GET /careerfit/families, the rule set's own family list. Mounted at /api/v1/careerfit, a prefix NO other rule in next.config.ts touches, so this flag can neither shadow nor be shadowed. NEW INFRASTRUCTURE this slice had to add, because a read must not score: ICareerFitRunReader / CareerFitRunReader (a persisted run read back on the CALLER's read-only RLS session) plus CareerFitRunJson.ParseInputQuality / ParseFamilyAudit, the inverses of the two serialisers FM-CF-010 wrote. No DDL, no new column, no policy, no GRANT. AUTH is the surrounding files' convention: RequireIdentity -> RequireSubscription -> CanAccessUser, denial as the uniform IDOR-safe 404; /families is authenticate-only (catalogue metadata, the treatment /vocational360/instrument gets). A run fetched BY ID re-runs CanAccessUser on the RUN'S OWNER — proven RED against the naive version that trusted RLS alone, which is exactly the hole CareerFitRlsTests.Same_school_caller_is_admitted_by_the_policy_so_the_endpoint_gate_is_not_optional names. NO FIT SCALAR REACHES A BROWSER: the ranking view carries the ordinal rank and the categorical gate/convergence/confidence labels only, and the assertion walks the raw JSON of every route for careerfit_absolute/career_fit_absolute/pca_index/mil_fit/*percent*/*probability* plus any property ending in _fit — the first draft listed only the persisted column spellings and stayed GREEN when the scalar was deliberately put back, which is why both spellings are pinned. THE FLAG IS NEW AND OFF: grep finds FORMMAPS_ROUTE_CAREERFIT_TO_DOTNET nowhere in the repo (.env.template, .github/workflows, any file) — the Vercel project's own environment could not be inspected from the worktree and is the one place left to confirm. Rewrite entries are PER-PATH with source == destination, never a /api/v1/careerfit/:path* prefix: a prefix silently adopts every route a later .NET commit adds under it, live on the next deploy with no flip and no canary (#109/#114/#120). DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: no legacy /api/v1/careers path is rewritten (shadow-then-replace is FM-CF-013 then FM-CF-015, not this slice), the F01–F23 ledger is not served over HTTP (~700 records per run; it is evidence for an auditor and rides on the run for FM-CF-013's in-process use), no audit_events row is written (the immutable run IS the audit record), and no DELETE or re-run-of-a-run is mapped (SELECT + INSERT only, dotnet-service-role.sql 4.7).
